messages:
lina: quick flagwe're seeing a reproducible MRR drop in the quantized reranker on the 'compact-candidates' cohort. ndcg@10 barely moves but top1 reliability tanked. anyone else?
omar: pulling numbers now. cohort = compact-candidates (avg doc len 18 tokens).
(later) omar: fp16 MRR 0.498 -> quant8 MRR 0.452. NDCG@10 fp16 0.781 -> quant8 0.774. drop concentrated in top1.
yu: interesting. if ndcg stable but top1 down, could be tie-breaking or score scaling issue. any change in dedupe or candidate shuffling?
lina: we recently switched dedupe to be "fuzzy-simple" (edit-distance threshold 0.2) vs previous exact URL dedupe. may affect candidate order for near-duplicates.
ara: I remember a small scoring change in the reranker postprocess: we scale logits by 1.0 for fp16 but applied quant-aware calibration factor 0.98 for quant builds to try to match distributions. maybe that backfired for top1.
joel: can we look at per-query score distributions? especially pair diffs between top2 and top1.
omar: grabbing sample distributions:
```
query q-789: top scores fp16 [0.87,0.65,0.64] -> quant [0.65,0.65,0.64]
query q-432: fp16 [0.72,0.71,0.33] -> quant [0.52,0.51,0.33]
```
om: some cases look like uniform downscale; others show top1 collapse, becoming tied with top2. tie-breaker currently uses candidate ingestion order.
yu: ingestion order nondeterminism + new fuzzy dedupe could flip which candidate wins ties. If quant scores compress, tie frequency increases -> MRR falls. NDCG less sensitive.
lina: action plan: 1) run eval with explicit deterministic tie-breaker (score then candidate_id) 2) run without the 0.98 calibration factor 3) try restoring exact-url dedupe for a subset to measure impact.
ara: also add a small synthetic test that injects micro-score gaps (0.01) to see how many become ties after quantization.
dev-bot: queued jobs: 1776010005 (deterministic-tiebreak), 1776010010 (no-calibration), 1776010015 (exact-dedupe). links: https://ci.redwood/evals/1776010000/
(later) omar: results mini-batch (10k):
- det-tiebreak quant8 MRR 0.472 (improved from 0.452)
- no-calib quant8 MRR 0.475
- exact-dedupe quant8 MRR 0.481
=> all mitigations recover some top1. exact dedupe recovers most.
yu: nice. suggests two interacting factors: quant score compression + fuzzy dedupe increasing tie/swap cases.
lina: longer-term: avoid fuzzy dedupe for onboarding cohorts and add quant-aware scoring normalization that preserves rank gaps. we should also add a regression test in rankbench: simulate quant noise and assert top1 stability >= 0.96 on small gold set.
ara: can we compute tie-rate per-cohort? shipping a small script: `python scripts/tie_rate.py --model quant8 --cohort compact-candidates`
joel: we should also surface candidate provenance in rerank logs so we can prefer canonical doc ids in tie-breaks.
lina: decided immediate fix = revert fuzzy dedupe for production candidate pipeline and remove the 0.98 calibration for quant8 until we implement a better calibration. I'll open the rollback PR.
omar: filing follow-ups:
- (omar) measure tie-rate delta across all cohorts and post csv
- (yu) add deterministic tie-break to eval harness and CI test
- (ara) build synthetic compression test and add to rankbench
- (lina) rollback fuzzy dedupe + remove quant calibration factor
dev-bot: linked issue https://tracker.redwood/INFR-1222 (rerank quant top1 regression)
joel: make sure to tag product if this affects search percetion for customers.
lina: pinging product: @product-team :warning: summary posted to ticket.
end of thread.
